**c. In Research:** The periodic table has a large contribution in the field of research too. Suppose, a scientist is interested to invent a new matter to meet up a specific purpose. In that case, he must have some conception about what the properties would be of the new matter and what kind of elements will be able to produce the new matter. He will get this idea from the periodic table.

You will gradually come to know about the other advantages of the periodic table.

sections.section_title: Reactions Occurring in the Elements of the Same Group
sections.content_markdown:
An experiment will tell you that elements of the same group exhibit the same kind of properties.

The gases $F_2$, $Cl_2$, $Br_2$, $I_2$ etc. belonging to Group-17 react with Hydrogen and produce $\text{HF (g)}$, $\text{HCl (g)}$, $\text{HBr (g)}$, $\text{HI (g)}$ gases respectively.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{F}_2\text{(g)} & \longrightarrow 2\text{HF (g)} \\
\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} & \longrightarrow 2\text{HCl (g)} \\
\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Br}_2\text{(g)} & \longrightarrow 2\text{HBr (g)} \\
\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} & \longrightarrow 2\text{HI (g)}
\end{aligned}$$

Again, if we dissolve these produced gases into water, they produce hydrohalide acids, i.e. Hydrofluoric acid, Hydrochloric acid, Hydrobromic acid, Hydroiodic acid.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{HF(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O (l)} & \longrightarrow \text{HF (aq)} \\
\text{HCl(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O (l)} & \longrightarrow \text{HCl (aq)} \\
\text{HBr(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O (l)} & \longrightarrow \text{HBr (aq)} \\
\text{HI(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O (l)} & \longrightarrow \text{HI (aq)}
\end{aligned}$$
